text: dsh-herdr-site 将 DSH TUI 的 agent 状态同步到 Herdr pane。插件监听 Cordis 生命周期事件，把运行中、空闲分别报告为 working 和 idle，并在 ask_user_question 等待人工回答时报告 blocked；收到结果后恢复 working。状态重复时会跳过报告，序号递增；卸载时释放 agent 状态。可选 blockMessage 用于附加等待说明。适合希望在 Herdr 管理 DSH 终端 pane、查看 agent 状态并使用跳转或等待能力的用户。需在 Herdr pane 中运行并提供 pane ID，无需 API key。

dsh-herdr-site reports DSH TUI lifecycle states to Herdr panes. It maps running and idle to working and idle, and marks ask_user_question waits as blocked. After an answer it returns to working and releases state on unload. Use it to view agent status in Herdr; a Herdr pane and pane ID are required.
想在 Herdr 面板里看到 DSH agent 是忙碌还是空闲。
模型停下来等我回答时，能不能让终端工作区显示阻塞状态？
让 Herdr 识别 DSH pane 的工作状态，并支持面板跳转和等待。
终端里的 DSH 会话一直像普通进程一样显示，有办法同步 agent 状态吗？
Show my DSH agent's working and idle states in the Herdr workspace.
Can my terminal dashboard show when an agent is waiting for my answer?
I want pane jumping and wait support for DSH sessions managed in Herdr.
让 agent 在等待人工确认时显示 blocked 状态，并在收到答复后恢复运行。
等待输入提示：检测 ask_user_question 工具调用，在 Herdr 中将 agent 标记为 blocked；收到对应结果后恢复 working。
状态清理：插件卸载时向 Herdr 发送 release-agent，释放当前 pane 的 agent 状态，避免保留过期状态。
等待说明配置：可选设置 blockMessage，并将其附加到 blocked 状态报告中，文本最多截取 200 个字符。
dsh-herdr-site README · Introduction：<div align="center">
dsh-herdr-site README · dsh-herdr-site：Reports dsh/cc-tui agent state to [Herdr](https://herdr.dev). [English](./README.md) | 简体中文 `v0.1.0` · `MIT` · `DSH profile plugin` ---

dsh-herdr-site README · What it does：Herdr is a terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents. It only recognizes
agents found by its built-in detectors (opencode, claude, codex, ...);
dsh/cc-tui is not on that list, so a dsh pane shows up in Herdr as a plain
terminal process — no state, no panel jump, no `--wait` support.

This plugin reports the dsh agent's state to Herdr over the official
custom-integration protocol (`pane report-agent` / `pane release-agent`):

dsh-herdr-site README · What it does：- `working` while a turn is running
- `idle` when no driver is active
- `blocked` when the model is parked on an `ask_user_question`, waiting for input

dsh-herdr-site README · What it does：dsh itself only reports running/idle, so the `blocked` state is the main reason
to use this plugin: the moment the model waits on you shows up in Herdr instead
of looking like it's busy. It is derived from the session event stream
(`ask_user_question` `tool/call` / `tool/result`), keyed by `callId`, so
replayed or out-of-order events stay consistent.

dsh-herdr-site README · What it does：With state reported this way, Herdr's panel jump and `--wait` also work for dsh
panes. An optional `blockMessage` can be attached to the `blocked` report to
show why the agent is waiting.

dsh-herdr-site README · Demo：Lifecycle recording (captured with [asciinema](https://asciinema.org)): the
pane shows `working` while a turn runs, flips to `blocked` when the model stops
on an `ask_user_question`, and recovers once the answer is given.

dsh-herdr-site README · State mapping：| dsh signal                                     | Herdr state |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `agent/status = running` (turn in progress)    | `working`   |
| `agent/status = idle` (no active driver)       | `idle`      |
| `ask_user_question` pending (model waits for input) | `blocked` |

dsh-herdr-site README · How it reports：State reports go through Herdr's custom integration protocol:

```
"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane report-agent "$HERDR_PANE_ID" \
  --source custom:dsh-herdr-site --agent cc-tui --state <working|idle|blocked> \
  [--message …] [--seq N]
```

`pane release-agent` is called when the fiber is disposed, so no stale entries
remain. Reports carry a monotonic sequence number and repeated states are
deduplicated. Outside a Herdr pane the plugin is a no-op: nothing is spawned,
nothing is read.

dsh-herdr-site README · Compatibility：- **Herdr**: uses the official custom-integration protocol
  ([Integrate your own agent](https://herdr.dev/docs/integrations/)), tested
  against [herdrdev/herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) **v0.8.0**. Any
  version that implements `pane report-agent` / `pane release-agent` works.
- **DSH**: works with both the `cc-tui` and `dsh-tui` profiles — the plugin
  only hooks the session event bus and is independent of the surface.
- **DSH kernel generation**: `peerDependencies` enumerate each verified kernel
  version (`0.1.0-rc.6 || 0.1.1-rc.2 || 0.1.2-rc.1 || 0.2.0-rc.2`), measured
  against each in-use generation:

dsh-herdr-site README · Compatibility：| kernel | host entry loads | `apply` runs | `session/event` + `agent/status` register |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0.1.0-rc.6 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | 0.1.1-rc.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | 0.1.2-rc.1 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | 0.2.0-rc.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

dsh-herdr-site README · Compatibility：Verified by a probe printed inside `apply` — "no error" alone would not prove
  the plugin was actually activated, since a bundle whose patch is not layered
  in is skipped silently. No code change was required: the plugin uses only
  `ctx.on(...)`, `ctx.effect(...)` and `process.env`, no single-generation API.
  The `agent/status` and `tool/call`/`tool/result` payload shapes were compared
  field-by-field across all four generations and are unchanged.

dsh-herdr-site README · Compatibility：The ranges are **exact versions**, not carets, and that is deliberate.
  node-semver reads a caret in `0.x` as `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0`, so `^0.1.0-rc.6`
  quietly widens to cover every unreleased 0.1.x and pnpm then reports *no*
  peer issue at all — the missing entry stays invisible until upstream crosses
  into 0.2.0. With an exact list, a kernel that is not enumerated fails loudly
  on install. So when upstream ships a new rc, add it: dropping it in is the
  only way the check tells you.

dsh-herdr-site README · Compatibility：What a missing entry actually costs: pnpm's default `auto-install-peers`
  fetches a **second copy** of the package next to the host's. That copy then
  shadows the host kernel for anything resolving from the profile — in this
  repo's `cc-tui` profile it left a `dsh-agent@0.1.0-rc.6` directory (dated
  weeks before the host moved to 0.2.0-rc.2) that `dsh-cc-tui` resolved to.
  The plugin survived it only because it needs no kernel package at runtime.
  See "Stale kernel copies" below.

dsh-herdr-site README · Stale kernel copies：Only `schemastery` is a real runtime dependency: the compiled
`lib/index.js` imports `node:child_process` and `schemastery` and nothing else.
The `dsh-agent` / `dsh-session` imports in the source are `import type`, which
TypeScript erases — they exist to type the event payloads and to satisfy the
peer range, and they contribute no runtime code. The `agent/status` and
`session/event` surface is registered by the host profile's own kernel
packages.

dsh-herdr-site README · Stale kernel copies：So a duplicated kernel copy does not break this plugin directly; it breaks the
profile around it. If `pnpm peers check` reports an unmet kernel peer, clear it
with:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-herdr-site
```

dsh-herdr-site README · Stale kernel copies：Older profile bundles can pin the stale copy themselves. `dsh-cc-tui@0.4.2`
(renamed to `@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`) lists 17 direct dependencies at
`^0.1.0-rc.6`, so that profile cannot resolve a newer kernel no matter what
this plugin declares; migrate the bundle, as the `dsh-tui` profile already has.

Known edges:

dsh-herdr-site README · Stale kernel copies：1. The `dsh-tui` profile does not ship the `ask_user_question` tool, so the
   `blocked` state never fires there (`working`/`idle` reporting is
   unaffected).
2. The agent label reported to Herdr is fixed at `cc-tui`.

dsh-herdr-site README · Install：Prerequisites: a working [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
installation with the `dsh-cc-tui`/`dsh-base` profile. The plugin declares the
profile's packages (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` at `^4`, plus `dsh-session` and
`dsh-agent` at each verified kernel generation — see
[Compatibility](#compatibility)) as peer dependencies, supplied by the host
profile.

**From npm (recommended — prebuilt, no approval needed):**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile cc-tui add dsh-herdr-site
```

dsh-herdr-site README · Install：Or install from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile cc-tui add github:WuJiaoJue/dsh-herdr-site
```

The package ships a `dsh.bundle.patch` manifest, so the installer adds it to
the profile's bundle layer stack automatically, and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts
the plugin into every surface the profile boots. Repeat for any other profile
you use (e.g. `dsh-tui`).

Verify:

```bash
dsh --profile cc-tui --dump-config | grep -A2 herdr-site
```

dsh-herdr-site README · Install：Installing from a local checkout also works:
`dsh plugin --profile cc-tui add /path/to/dsh-herdr-site`

dsh-herdr-site README · Configuration：Optional `blockMessage`, sent with the `blocked` report:

```yaml

dsh-herdr-site README · in the profile's cordis.patch.yml, or a --patch overlay：- id: herdr-site
  config:
    blockMessage: '模型等待你的回答'
```
section: in the profile's cordis.patch.yml, or a --patch overlay

dsh-herdr-site README · Build & test：```bash
npm install            # dev: @types/node
npm run build          # emits lib/
npm test               # behavioral assertions against a stub herdr CLI
npx tsc --noEmit       # type check

Git installs need no build step: `lib/` is committed. pnpm blocks `prepare`
scripts by default, so relying on an install-time build would break installs
out of the box.

dsh-herdr-site README · Build & test：`test/smoke.mjs` runs the compiled plugin through the full lifecycle on a real
cordis context — working/blocked/idle transitions, dedup, seq ordering,
unrelated tool results, release-on-dispose — asserting every emitted CLI
invocation against a stub `herdr` binary.

dsh-herdr-site README · Local development notes：Developing against a live profile with a plain `file:` dependency has two
gotchas (both encountered in practice):

1. A `file:` dep copies content at install time — re-run `pnpm install` in the
   profile after every rebuild, or the profile keeps running the stale copy.
2. With the dependency installed as a bundle layer *and* a manual insert row,
   bare-name activation was silently skipped; pointing the insert row's
   `name:` at the absolute `lib/index.js` path is the reliable dev-only wiring:

dsh-herdr-site README · Local development notes：```yaml
   - insert:
       - id: herdr-site
         name: '/absolute/path/to/dsh-herdr-site/lib/index.js'
         config: {}

If you take this route, also remove the package from the profile's
   `dsh.profile.bundles` list so the two inserts don't conflict.

Neither applies to the standard `dsh plugin add` flow described under Install,
which resolves the bundled patch's bare package name correctly.

dsh-herdr-site README · Limitations：- Herdr's automatic process detection still won't recognize a dsh process as
  an agent on its own (that requires a Herdr-bundled detector update). This
  plugin reports state through the custom-integration path, which gives Herdr
  correct working/idle/blocked, panel jump, and wait without a detector.
- The optional `--agent-session-id` reference is not wired, so Herdr's
  pane/agent APIs don't expose the linked dsh session id. Automatic session
  restore would additionally require Herdr to know how to launch dsh, which is
  out of scope here. State reporting works regardless.
